sn_aia_agent.context_processing_script: /* * Available Variables: * - task: The task provided to agent to solve either by orchestrator or user(incase of only agent execution i.e agent is invoked as seperate entity instead from a workflow). * - user_utterance: The user utterance provided. and task = user_utterance in case of individual agent execution. * - agent_id: The agent id. * - context: An object that carries additional contextual information for the agent. * It always includes a "pageContext" and may include a "triggerContext", * depending on how and from where the agent is invoked. * * Behavior by invocation type: * --------------------------------- * - When invoked via the startAiAgentConversation API: * If a "contextMemory" parameter is provided in the API request, * it will be available here as the "triggerContext". * The "pageContext" is always present in this call, regardless * of whether the agent is executed individually or as part of a use case. * Example: * { * pageContext: { ... }, * triggerContext: { ... } // Derived from contextMemory (if passed) * } * * - When invoked as part of a use case or workflow: * The "pageContext" and "triggerContext" objects available here * may have been *modified* by the use case’s context processing script. * This means the use case may alter, extend, or overwrite values * from the original "pageContext" or "triggerContext" * before the context reaches the agent. * If the use case was originally triggered via the API, * the initial "triggerContext" is still derived from the * "contextMemory" parameter, but its contents may have been updated * by the use case logic. * * - When executed directly (standalone agent execution): * The "pageContext" will always be present (default or empty), * and the "triggerContext" will only be populated if explicitly * passed through the API call. * Return an modified context like: { pageContext : {},triggerContext:{} } */ (function(task, user_utterance, agent_id, context) { return { pageContext : context?.pageContext, triggerContext : context?.triggerContext }; })(task,user_utterance, agent_id, context);
sn_aia_agent.description: Assistant scoped to Forecast Variance that exposes the platform Build Agent skill family (Build Agent, Build Agent Preprocessor, BA Glide Tools Metadata Summarizer) for use in the WDF Lab.
sn_aia_agent.instructions: You have three tools, each wrapping a native platform Build Agent skill: "Build Agent", "Build Agent Preprocessor", and "BA Glide Tools Metadata Summarizer". When the user asks for something Build Agent would normally do inside Studio (generate/preprocess app metadata, summarize Glide Tools metadata), call the matching tool and return its result plainly.
sn_aia_agent.name: Build Agent Skills Assistant
sn_aia_agent.proficiency: - Serves as a specialized Build Agent Skills Assistant that provides comprehensive support for Build Agent operations within the Studio platform, acting as an intermediary to access and utilize native Build Agent skills and functionalities for application development workflows. - Generates application metadata through the native Build Agent tool, enabling the creation and structuring of app-level information required for Studio application development by processing user requests and invoking the underlying Build Agent skill to produce metadata outputs. - Preprocesses application metadata using the Build Agent Preprocessor tool, performing preliminary analysis, validation, and transformation of app metadata inputs to prepare them for subsequent Build Agent operations and ensure data quality and compatibility within the Studio environment. - Summarizes Glide Tools metadata through the BA Glide Tools Metadata Summarizer tool, providing concise and structured overviews of Glide Tools metadata information to help users understand tool capabilities, configurations, and metadata structures within the Build Agent ecosystem. - Interprets and routes user requests for Build Agent operations by analyzing the nature of the task (whether it involves metadata generation, preprocessing, or Glide Tools summarization), selecting the appropriate native platform tool from the available Build Agent skills, executing the tool, and returning the results in a plain, accessible format to the user. - Provides seamless integration with Studio's native Build Agent platform skills, acting as a wrapper interface that enables users to access powerful Build Agent functionalities including metadata generation, preprocessing, and Glide Tools analysis without requiring direct interaction with the underlying platform complexities.
